To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) mutual information is useful for adaptively selecting the items for a test; (2) a mutual information criterion can be used to select items for a test that are more likely to reveal students' knowledge than items selected by a traditional criterion, such as the item-total correlation; and (3) the performance of a test based on a mutual information criterion improves as the number of items increases.

mutual information is an effective and efficient measure for adaptive test item selection, and that the mutual information-based approach outperforms the current state of the art in adaptive test item selection.
